sequence_description: JWT M2M: configure two OAuth Sources (one intended, one attacker-controlled) and test whether JWT login incorrectly accepts attacker-signed tokens due to overly-broad trust anchor selection (jwks_sources confusion).
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_attacker_other_source_jwt_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_attacker_other_source_jwt_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: JWT login accepted a token signed by a different (attacker-controlled) configured source; verification policy may be broader than the intended semantic trust anchor.

sequence_description: JWT trust-anchor rotation coherence: baseline JWT login succeeds with Source A JWKS; then update the OAuth Source JWKS URL (simulating key rotation) and re-save; old-key JWT should be rejected after the update.
description:
Assertion FAILED: old_key_login_http_status >= 400
Evaluation: old_key_login_http_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: After explicit JWKS update/re-save, authentik still accepted a JWT signed by the old key, indicating stale trust-anchor usage (config/runtime incoherence).

sequence_description: Config-change coherence: obtain a token with broader scope, then tighten the application configuration and re-authenticate requesting the same scope; the tightened config should take effect immediately and reject/limit the flow.
description:
Assertion FAILED: user_tighten_after_login_status >= 400
Evaluation: user_tighten_after_login_status=200 >= 400 → False
Implication: After tightening application policy_engine_mode, re-authentication still succeeded as if old configuration was cached/stale (config-change flow coherence failure).

sequence_description: JWT M2M exp enforcement as authorization boundary: first a control JWT with exp in the future should succeed, then an expired JWT (exp in the past) should be rejected; acceptance would allow unauthorized continued access beyond intended lifetime.
description: OIDC source login succeeded despite id_token issuer mismatch: the IdP returned an id_token with a different issuer than the source's configured OIDC well-known URL. This indicates the SP does not validate the iss claim per OIDC Core 3.1.3.7 Section 2.
